title: Conjecture 1 (Felsner et al.)
statement_text: The arrangement graph of every simple arrangement of great-circles on the sphere is 3-colorable.
context_text: Stated by Felsner, Hurtado, Noy, and Streinu in 2000 while studying connectivity, Hamiltonicity, and colorability of pseudoline and pseudocircle arrangement graphs. It is fairly well known but had seen little progress for 20 years prior to this paper.
paper_contribution: Verifies the conjecture for all $\triangle$-saturated pseudocircle arrangements (where one color class of the 2-coloring of faces consists of triangles only), for further classes of (pseudo-)circle arrangements, and computationally for all arrangements of up to 11 great-pseudocircles including non-realizable ones.
paper_title: Coloring circle arrangements: New $4$-chromatic planar graphs

title: Gimbel–Kundgen–Li–Thomassen Conjecture (Conjecture 3.2)
statement_text: Every 4-chromatic planar graph has fractional chromatic number strictly greater than $3$.
context_text: Conjectured by Gimbel, Kundgen, Li, and Thomassen in their work on the fractional chromatic number of planar graphs; they argued that a positive resolution would yield an alternative proof of the Four Color Theorem.
paper_contribution: Disproves the conjecture in a strong form by constructing an infinite family of 4-edge-critical 4-regular planar graphs that are fractionally 3-colorable.
paper_title: Coloring circle arrangements: New $4$-chromatic planar graphs

title: Belief on 4-vertex-critical arrangement graphs
statement_text: We believe that the corona construction (which extends a $\triangle$-saturated arrangement of pseudocircles with a pentagonal cell to a 4-chromatic arrangement by inserting one additional pseudocircle around the pentagonal cell) results in infinitely many 4-vertex-critical arrangement graphs.
context_text: An arrangement of pseudocircles is a family of simple closed curves on the sphere or in the plane, every two of which intersect at most twice. It is simple if no three curves share a point, and intersecting if every two curves intersect. Its arrangement graph is the planar graph whose vertices are the intersection points, with the curves subdivided into edges; for simple arrangements it is 4-regular, hence 4-colourable. A plane graph is $\triangle$-saturated if every edge is incident to exactly one triangular face, and an arrangement is $\triangle$-saturated if its arrangement graph is; the authors show that $\triangle$-saturated intersecting arrangements are 3-colourable. A $k$-chromatic graph is $k$-vertex-critical if deleting any vertex lowers the chromatic number, and $k$-edge-critical if deleting any edge does. The corona extension starts from a $\triangle$-saturated arrangement with a pentagonal cell. It inserts one new pseudocircle around the pentagon, crossing only the five pseudocircles bounding it, at edges incident to the pentagon's vertices. In the resulting 4-regular graph one face class consists of triangles and one pentagon, which forces independence number below $|V|/3$ and hence chromatic number 4. This gives an infinite family of 4-chromatic arrangements; Koester's arrangement of 7 circles, a 4-edge-critical 4-regular planar graph, arises this way. Because of similarities with Koester's crowning operation, the authors believe that many of these arrangement graphs are 4-vertex-critical. They prove a sufficient condition: if the arrangement graph is the medial graph of a cubic planar graph $H$ with a pentagonal face and a trihamiltonian 3-edge-colouring (each pair of colour classes forms a Hamiltonian cycle), then the corona extension is 4-vertex-critical, and even 4-edge-critical if $H$ has 5-fold rotational symmetry about the pentagon. They conjecture separately that there is an infinite family of 4-edge-critical simple arrangements of pseudocircles.
notes: Statement appears as running prose in the outline of Section 3; the exact family is defined later in that section, which is only partially present in the extracted text.
paper_title: Coloring circle arrangements: New $4$-chromatic planar graphs
